items.title: Asian markets follow Wall Street: Nikkei, Kospi jump up to 8% as Jensen Huang’s return sparks rally in AI stocks
points: Asian equities staged a powerful rebound on Tuesday, 24 November, tracking a sharp rally on Wall Street as renewed optimism around the artificial intelligence (AI) trade lifted technology stocks.
MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan jumped 4.6%, recovering from an eight-month low and heading for its biggest single-day advance in two weeks.
Japan's Nikkei 225 climbed 4.5% as trading resumed after a local market holiday.
South Korea's KOSPI rallied 7.5%, while Taiwan's benchmark index soared 9.1%, reflecting the strong recovery in technology-heavy markets.
The gains followed an extraordinary session on Wall Street, where Nvidia shares soared 31.5% on Monday.
The Nasdaq 100, which has significant exposure to large technology companies, jumped more than 6% on Monday.
The S&P 500 gained 4.7%, while the Nasdaq Composite surged 6.5%.
S&P 500 futures were largely unchanged early on Tuesday, while Nasdaq futures slipped 0.2%, indicating that investors were assessing the sustainability of the previous session's rally.

items.title: Nasscom seeks AI transformation scheme for IT firms in Budget 2027-28
points: The National Association of Software and Service Companies (Nasscom) has asked the government to set up a dedicated scheme to help Indian IT services companies adapt to artificial intelligence (AI).
This demand is part of its pre-budget recommendations for the Union Budget 2027-28.
The industry body said generative and agentic AI are changing what clients want, how technology work is delivered and how IT firms charge for it.
Building new AI products and retraining staff needs money upfront, it said, and companies have to spend it while still delivering for existing clients.
Nasscom wants the budget to commit to an “AI Services Transformation and Innovation Scheme” for an initial three years.
Under the proposal, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and the finance ministry would design the funding and implementation together with industry.

items.title: India’s rupee has become an accidental carry star
points: The Reserve Bank of India has made moves that temporarily attract carry traders to the rupee.
Recent factors include decreasing oil prices and a shift in foreign investment from artificial intelligence stocks to Indian markets.
However, these RBI incentives may not last, leaving uncertainty for traders.
India's interest rate advantage has significantly diminished since 2011, raising concerns.

items.title: Pune techie allegedly punches girlfriend to death, calls police for ambulance hours later
points: A 31-year-old software engineer has been arrested for allegedly murdering his 26-year-old friend, Komal Dahale, following an argument at her paying guest (PG) accommodation in Pune's Hinjewadi area in the early hours of Monday.
Dahale, a native of Wardha district in Maharashtra's Vidarbha region, was allegedly assaulted by the accused, Shubham Kalbande, during a dispute at her accommodation in Sakhare Vasti, police said.
Both Dahale and Kalbande worked as software engineers at two major IT companies in Pune and had known each other for around three-and-a-half years.
The Pimpri-Chinchwad police have arrested Kalbande and booked him for murder under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
The disagreement allegedly escalated into physical assault around 3 am, when Kalbande punched and assaulted Dahale repeatedly with his hands.
Around 6.30 am, Kalbande allegedly found Dahale unresponsive and called the police, seeking an ambulance.
Pimpri-Chinchwad police commissioner Vinoy Kumar Choubey confirmed that both the victim and the accused were IT professionals employed at different multinational companies.

items.title: IRCTC trials smaller menus on long-haul trains in quality push
points: Passengers on three Vande Bharat sleepers are being served a trimmed menu as part of a pilot project that cuts the number of items served for breakfast, lunch and dinner in a move officials said was aimed at improving the quality of food on trains.

The Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) introduced the compact menu, similar to meals offered on flights, on November 1 as part of an effort to address complaints about food quality and hygiene on long-distance trains, said officials.
The railways have contended with a flurry of complaints over poor food, said IRCTC officials from the agency’s West Zone, which covers parts of Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Goa.
The number of complaints has dropped 10% since the cloud kitchens began supplying meals, said Gaurav Jha, group general manager, IRCTC, West Zone, Mumbai.

items.title: UN urges probe after Russian ship attacked off Libya
points: The United Nations called on Monday (Nov 23) for an independent probe into drone attacks on two ships off Libya, including a Russian vessel, in a suspected spillover from the Ukraine war.

Libya Alhadath television reported later that naval and air force units intercepted more than 12 “explosive-laden sea drones” off Benghazi.

items.title: HMM signs green shipping deal with Nextpower
points: South Korean shipping company HMM said Monday it had signed a deal allowing US solar technology company Nextpower to reflect emissions reductions from HMM’s use of lower-carbon marine fuels in its supply chain emissions reporting.

Under its Green Sailing Service, HMM uses lower-carbon fuels and passes the resulting emissions reductions on to cargo customers for use in their Scope 3 reporting, which covers indirect emissions across a company’s value chain.
The agreements allow HMM to recover part of the cost of using lower-carbon fuels, helping fund further investments in lower-emission shipping.
Nextpower, which is listed on the Nasdaq, specializes in large-scale solar power systems and smart energy solutions.
The service follows the Global Maritime Forum’s principle of additionality.
Reductions made to comply with regulations, including those in the European Union, are ineligible.
The Nextpower agreement follows similar deals with German logistics company Hellmann in 2023, Swedish furniture retailer Ikea in 2024 and US sportswear company Nike in 2025.

items.title: Spain to Ban Ship Scrubber Wastewater Discharges Starting July 2027
points: Spain will ban wastewater discharges from ship exhaust gas cleaning systems, commonly known as scrubbers, in its ports and internal waters beginning July 1, 2027, imposing restrictions that go beyond existing regional environmental requirements.
The measure, established under Royal Decree 1006/2026 and published November 20, applies to all civilian vessels regardless of flag.
Scrubbers allow ships to meet International Maritime Organization (IMO) sulfur emissions limits while continuing to burn higher-sulfur fuel oil.
The new rules implement a 2025 decision by the OSPAR Commission, which oversees marine environmental protection in the Northeast Atlantic.

That agreement requires participating countries to prohibit open-loop scrubber discharges in ports and internal waters by July 2027, with restrictions extending to all scrubber operating modes by July 2029.
Scrubber-equipped ships must notify Spanish authorities of their systems at least 24 hours before arrival, or upon departure from the previous port for shorter voyages.

The remaining contribution comes from sunrise sectors such as data centres, EVs, defence and solar, which are currently relatively small in size but offer meaningful long-term opportunities.
We note: (1) Polycab’s diversified product portfolio, strong distribution network and leadership provide a competitive advantage.
(2) Emerging opportunities in data centres, solar inverters, battery storage and EHV cables offer additional growth levers.
(3) However, near-term volume growth could remain volatile due to elevated base effect and copper price movements, which may impact channel restocking.
(4) Competition from the new entrant remains a key monitorable, although we do not see any material near-term impact on its market share or pricing strategy.
We maintain our Add rating with a DCF-based revised TP of ₹8,300 (₹9,335 earlier), implying a target P/E of 32x FY28E EPS.

items.title: US Navy Plans 600-Ton Hypersonic Launcher For 12 Missiles On Destroyer USS Michael Monsoor
points: USS Michael Monsoor would receive a 600-ton launch module for hypersonic missiles under a US Navy plan to turn the Zumwalt-class destroyer into a long-range strike ship.
Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA) published two notices on November 17, 2026, which set out the industrial requirements for the work.
One notice covers the installation of the Large Missile Vertical Launch System (LMVLS), while the other announces an industry meeting in Washington on December 9.
The modernization period for the second ship of the Zumwalt class is planned from May 2028 till August 2030.
The prefabricated module for USS Michael Monsoor would measure around 13.6 metres long, 6.3 metres wide and 12.5 metres high.
Its four large launch tubes would hold up to 12 Conventional Prompt Strike (CPS) hypersonic missiles, with three missiles carried in each tube.
A Government Accountability Office report from July 2026 found that the effort to modernize all three Zumwalt-class destroyers for the missile was running 24 months behind schedule.

items.title: China’s Largest Home-Built Cruise Ship Begins Maiden Voyage With Over 3,800 Passengers
points: Cruise ship Adora Flora City began its maiden commercial voyage from Guangzhou in southern China on November 22 with more than 3,800 passengers on board.
The vessel is only the second large cruise ship to be built in China, and it set sail from the Nansha International Cruise Home Port in Guangdong Province.
Adora Flora City is reportedly scheduled to operate more than 50 international voyages from Guangzhou in 2027, which would range from short getaways to longer cruises across Southeast Asia.
The ship was built by Shanghai Waigaoqiao Shipbuilding, which is a subsidiary of China State Shipbuilding Corporation (CSSC).
It was handed over to its operator, Adora Cruises at the shipyard in Shanghai on November 6.
Adora Flora City has a gross tonnage of 141,900 and measures 341 metres in length, which makes it 17.4 metres longer than its sister ship Adora Magic City.
The shipyard said that overall construction efficiency improved by about 20% compared with Adora Magic City, which was China’s first domestically built large cruise ship.

items.title: Deleted voters’ appeals to get priority, Supreme Court tells Bengal SIR tribunals
points: A bench, comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, directed the tribunals to segregate the appeals into two categories, observing that challenges by deleted voters carried greater urgency as their right…

The bench further directed that appeals filed by deleted voters from constituencies falling within the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) limits be given priority, in view of the upcoming municipal elections.
Of the 38.31 lakh appeals filed so far, 22.21 lakh are by voters seeking restoration of their deleted names, while 16.10 lakh challenge the inclusion of certain voters in the electoral rolls.
Advocate Prashant Bhushan, appearing for petitioners, pointed out that although nearly 38 lakh appeals were filed, only a little over one lakh were decided so far.
He told the bench that 93% of the appeals decided had gone in favour of deleted voters.

items.title: French Salvors Struggle To Refloat 169m Bulk Carrier Miro G Stuck On Beach With 100 Tonnes Of Diesel
points: Bulk carrier Miro G has been stranded on a beach in southwest France since early November 20, 2026 as salvors wait for a chance to refloat it.
The 169-metre vessel was sailing without cargo but carries just over 100 tonnes of diesel fuel for its engines.
The ship had left Egypt on October 13 and was heading to the French port of Rouen.
An emergency anchoring was attempted off the coast, but gusts of about 90 km/h made the ship drag its anchor towards the beach.
The Miro G grounded shortly after midnight on Friday with 22 seafarers on board.
A French Air and Space Force helicopter airlifted 19 of them to safety while the captain and two crew members stayed on the ship to help with the operations.
Shallow water means the tug cannot get closer than about 900 metres to the Miro G on the beach.

items.title: Sanctioned Russian Cargo Ship Sparta II Hit By Drones In Gulf Of Finland Towed Out Of Finnish Waters
points: Russian cargo ship Sparta II has been towed out of Finnish waters after a drone attack in the Gulf of Finland left it burning and adrift.
A Russian rescue vessel began towing the damaged ship on the afternoon of November 22, 2026, after two days of firefighting.
Finland’s Border Guard said the tow ended its rescue mission once the ship had left the Finnish economic zone.
The Sparta II was sailing to the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad when it was hit on the morning of November 21.
Finnish authorities were alerted at around 8:50 am local time and located the ship about 50 km west of Suursaari island in the eastern Gulf of Finland.
According to the Finnish Defence Forces, Ukraine was likely behind the attack, though Ukraine has not commented on it as of November 23, Sunday.
The US sanctioned the Sparta II in 2022, and Ukraine added it to its own sanctions list this year.

items.title: Indonesian Navy Seizes Bangladesh-Bound Ship Carrying 405 Tonnes Of Rocket-Grade Chemicals And Millions Of SIM Cards
points: Cargo ship MV Star Line has been seized by the Indonesian Navy while it was carrying 405 tonnes of the rocket-grade chemical sodium perchlorate to Bangladesh.
The Comoros-flagged vessel was stopped on November 7, 2026, in the waters off Belawan in Indonesia’s North Sumatra province.
Details of the seizure were made public only on November 20 at a press briefing held by naval officials in Belawan.
The general cargo ship had sailed from Lianyungang in China and was bound for Mongla Port in Bangladesh, where it was supposed to arrive on November 8.

On the way, it made an unscheduled stop in Indonesian waters, reportedly to take on fuel, when the crew of the patrol vessel KRI Sigalu-857 spotted the cargo ship moving in an odd pattern away from its designated route.
Out of the 36 containers on board the Star Line, as many as 15 were loaded with the chemical.
The navy team reportedly also came across 54 pallets of unregistered blank 4G SIM cards, which ran into millions.

US Navy Awards $7.125 Billion Contract To 28 Companies To Modernise Electronic Warfare Systems On Its Ships
points: The U.S Navy has awarded a $7.125 billion indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract to 28 companies, after getting 31 offers, in an effort to modernise naval electronic warfare systems.

The scope of the agreement extends to US warships, including Coast Guard vessels and support platforms operated by allied nations as part of the Surface Electronic Warfare Improvement Program (SEWIP).

The SEWIP includes a network of systems built to enhance a ship’s detection and protection capabilities by offering threat detection at the initial stage, accurate signal analysis, alert generation in response to potential attacks and safeguard against…
In this way, the Navy seeks to boost its surveillance and improve the fleet’s response to threats.

A few of the selected companies include Lockheed Martin, Raytheon, HII Mission Technologies, General Dynamics Mission Systems Inc, Northrop Grumman, BAE Systems Technology Solutions & Services Inc and others.
Additionally, the $7.125 billion is the contract ceiling and not the immediate disbursement or a distribution of the tasks among the selected companies.

items.title: Bengal govt to change state’s English name to Paschim Banga; 8 bills lined up in assembly
points: ‘Paschim Banga’ will be the official English name of the eastern state, chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Monday, adding that the resolution to rename the state will be tabled in the assembly during the next session beginning on December 4.
“Our government will present eight bills related to various departments during a 10-day session of the legislative assembly starting December 4.
On December 9, we will present a bill proposing that the state’s English name, West Bengal, be changed to Paschim Banga.
The Bengali name will be written in English alphabet once the bill is passed,” Adhikari told the media after the cabinet meeting at Nabanna, the state secretariat.
The names West Bengal and Paschim Banga were established during the 1947 Partition when the eastern part of the undivided Bengal province was separated to form East Pakistan.
When asked what would happen with cows taken to licensed slaughter houses, Adhikari said the state will strictly follow the West Bengal Animal Slaughter Control Act, 1950.

items.title: Video of excavator near high-risk Sheshnag Lake in J&K sparks outrage, leaders seek halt on activity
points: A purported video showing an excavator deployed near the high-altitude Sheshnag Lake, a high-risk glacial lake, in Jammu and Kashmir's Anantnag district has sparked widespread outrage, with political parties, religious leaders, and environmentalists…

The video, which went viral on social media, shows heavy machinery operating in close proximity to the pristine glacial water body along the traditional Amarnath Yatra pilgrimage route in the south Kashmir Himalayas.
Sheshnag Lake is among the 14 high-risk glacial lakes identified across Jammu and Kashmir that are closely monitored for environmental vulnerabilities.
National Conference (NC) Lok Sabha MP Mian Altaf said it is essential to safeguard Kashmir's lakes.
Former Lok Sabha MP from Srinagar, Ruhullah Mehdi, said Kashmir's mountains are not the BJP's real estate.
Now heavy machinery is digging at Sheshnag, a high-risk glacial lake.
" It is already listed among the 14 high-risk glacial lakes in Jammu and Kashmir.

items.title: US Navy Proposes 15 New Trump- Class Battleships For $275 Billion To Replace DDG(X) Destroyer Program
points: The U.S. Navy is planning to replace the DDG (X) destroyer program and build 15 Trump-class nuclear-powered battleships, each with a displacement of around 35,000 tons, according to a Congressional Budget Office (CBO) review of the Navy’s 2027 shipbuilding…
The first or lead battleship of the Trump-class would be procured in 2028, with an average of roughly one ship every two years through 2056.

The vessel would cost nearly $23.4 billion, with the other 14 expected to be around $18 billion each, bringing the total cost of the 15 ships to an estimated $275 billion, excluding research and development expenditure.
The ships designated BBGN would be one of the largest surface combatants ever built by the U.S. Navy since the Iowa-class.
Sources suggest that each ship would be fitted with 128 Mk 41 Vertical Launch System Cells alongside 12 Conventional Prompt Strike Hypersonic Missiles in 4 large launch tubes.

items.title: Russia’s Northern Sea Route Breaks 40 Million-Tonne Barrier For First Time, but Putin’s Ambitions Remain Out of Reach
points: Nuclear icebreaker Vaygach escorting a convoy of crude oil and oil product tankers along the Northern Sea Route in July 2024.
(Source: Atomflot) Cargo volumes along Russia’s Northern Sea Route (NSR) have surpassed 40 million tonnes for the first time, setting a new record for the Arctic shipping corridor.
The milestone marks continued growth in Russian Arctic shipping, although volumes remain far below the ambitious targets set forth by President Vladimir Putin over the past decade.
Rosatom chief executive Alexey Likhachev said cargo transportation crossed the 40-million-tonne threshold on November 17.
Over the past five years, annual cargo volumes have increased from 34.87 million tonnes in 2021 to more than 40 million tonnes in 2026, an increase of roughly 15%.
Transit volumes reached 6 million tonnes by early November, twice the level recorded during the same period last year, according to Russian Arctic Development Minister Alexey Chekunkov.

items.title: Fake Iran Tanker Highlights Uncertainty Around Hormuz Traffic
points: Oil/Chemical Tanker "Bald Man" at the Port of Fujairah, as the U.S. -Israel conflict with Iran limits marine traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, in Fujairah, United Arab Emirates, May 6, 2026.

A vessel purporting to be the Khat Shekan, an Iranian very large crude carrier, appeared on Sunday on some ship-tracking platforms including MarineTraffic, indicating it was beginning an exit from the Persian Gulf.
The catch is that the position is very likely fake and the ship — whose name translates as “Line Breaker” — may not exist at all, according to analysts and maritime tracking experts.

“Any attempts to complicate the monitoring of traffic through the Strait of Hormuz are an unwelcome addition to an already dangerous situation,” said Mark Douglas, an analyst at ship-tracking platform Starboard Maritime Intelligence.

The signals suggest the vessel is a laden crude tanker heading for China’s Zhoushan port, but it has no International Maritime Organization number, a unique identifier for vessels that remains through their operational life.

items.title: Ukraine Sinks Russian Warship in Libya as Conflict Spreads Beyond Europe
points: The Russian cargo ship Sparta II during fire extinguishing at a location given as the Gulf of Finland, November 21, 2026.

Nov 23 (Reuters) – Ukraine sank a Russian naval corvette in a Libyan port using naval drones on Sunday, the day after a drone strike on a Russian military-linked cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said.
Zelenskiy said on Monday morning that Ukraine used seven naval drones in Sunday’s attack, and had also hit the Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara, which he said Russia had used to transport weapons.

“Despite all the enemy’s attempts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette ‘Mercury‘ was sunk,” Zelenskiy posted on Telegram, the first official acknowledgement that Ukraine has carried out an attack in Libya.
Zelenskiy said a Russian Ka-27 combat helicopter had been destroyed along with the corvette.

items.title: US Navy Rejects Push To Rename Next Aircraft Carrier Slated To Honour Pearl Harbor Hero Doris Miller After Trump
points: The U.S. Navy does not plan to rename the next Ford-class aircraft carrier currently under construction after the U.S. President Donald Trump.

The Navy had also recommended Miller for the Medal of Honor, however, whether he would be given the country’s highest military decoration depends on the decision of Congress and approval of President Donald Trump.
Doris or ‘Dorrie’ Miller enlisted in the U.S Navy in 1939 during the Second World War.
When the Japanese attacked Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941, Miller was a Mess Attendant of the Third Class on the USS West Virginia.
Miller died in November 1943 during the Battle of Makin when the aircraft carrier USS Liscome was torpedoed by a Japanese submarine.

During the first term of President Donald Trump, the Navy had announced that the new aircraft carrier would be called USS Doris Miller, in the honour of an enlisted sailor who assisted the U.S forces during the Japanese attack.

items.title: Australia Rejects Budget Office Report Claiming AUKUS Submarine Deal Could Weaken U.S Navy
points: The Defense Minister of Australia Richard Marles rejected claims that the AUKUS Deal to provide nuclear submarines to Canberra could weaken the U.S Navy for years to come.

The concerns were mentioned in a report by the US Congressional Budget Office which warned that AUKUS could put pressure on American submarine production capacity, per the Australian Broadcasting Corporation.
The report which was released on Thursday, stated that building submarines for Australia would add to the production challenges being faced by the U.S Shipyards.
Under the AUKUS Agreement forged in 2021, Australia, Britain and U.S are working together to develop nuclear powered submarines for the naval fleet of Canberra.

For this purpose, the U.K has promised an investment of around £4 billion or $5.3 billion, the US is providing $17.5 billion, and Australia is pouring over 30 billion Australian dollars or $20.7 billion.
U.S President Donald Trump said he wouldn’t allow this and threatened the companies of high taxes if they decided to move forward in this direction.

items.title: Google Reveals What Indians Want From Their Holidays in 2026, and It's Not Just Popular Tourist Spots

Google has revealed what Indians have been searching for when planning their holidays in 2026.
The company also seems to have seen a sharp rise in searches for AI-powered travel planning over the past year, as more people turn to these tools to research and organise their trips.
Google has found growing interest in outdoor activities and live events among people planning trips in India, the company said in a blog post.
Interest in lesser-known destinations has also picked up, with searches for "hidden gems india" rising by 400 percent, according to Google Trends data.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Reaches Day One Sales of $3.79 Billion, Shatters Entertainment Records
points: GTA 6's day one haul of $3.79 billion beats the lifetime earnings of top-grossing films like Avengers: Endgame, Avatar, and Spider-Man: Brand New Day.
Grand Theft Auto 6 was expected to become the biggest entertainment launch in history, and now it has.
Publisher Take-Two and developer Rockstar Games have confirmed that the game's day one retail sales reached $3.79 billion, shattering box office records in the entertainment industry.
The sales figures are based on company estimates through end of day November 19 worldwide, Take Two confirmed in a press release.
Sales numbers have surely gone further up since Grand Theft Auto 6 launched last week.
The game's haul of $3.79 billion on launch day itself beats the lifetime earnings of top-grossing films like Avengers: Endgame, Avatar, and Spider-Man: Brand New Day.
It has also convincingly beaten its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto 5, which reached $1 billion in sales in three days.
Rockstar's last game, Red Dead Redemption 2, generated $725 million in sales from its opening weekend.
